topics.label: 2023 Hiroshima Smart Agriculture Project
topics.description:
The 2023 Hiroshima Smart Agriculture Project is the acknowledged parent framework for the recorded citrus drone research in Hiroshima Prefecture. The paper names its purpose as construction of an efficient integrated system for large-scale management of lemon and other crops. Its documented connection here is the water-spraying study, which tested aircraft control and canopy deposition.

The acknowledgment establishes that project relationship; it does not describe the parent project’s complete work programme, administration, budget, other trials or overall results. Those details are not reported in the reviewed material. Results from the citrus study remain attached to that study and its two trial variants rather than being presented as an evaluation of the entire parent project. This record describes the framework acknowledged in a paper published in March 2024 and does not assess present project activity or funding eligibility.

topics.label: Citrus drone spraying experiment
topics.description:
A water-only citrus canopy-spraying study evaluated a drone supplied continuously with electricity and water from the ground. It addressed the need for longer, higher-pressure orchard spraying and tested RTK-GNSS positioning with a propeller-tilt mechanism to counter spray recoil. The research was carried out under the 2023 Hiroshima Smart Agriculture Project, with an automatic trial at Innoshima on 19 September and a manual trial at Ikuchijima on 20 September 2023.

The authors reported stable attitude and accurate position control during spraying. The automatic flight followed its planned route; the manual trial used a crawler vehicle to carry the hose and cable, and water-sensitive paper showed good spray adhesion. These are results for aircraft operation and canopy deposition, not measurements of root-zone wetting, establishment irrigation, carob survival or labour savings. Takeoff and landing remained manual in the automatic trial to avoid entanglement. Published on 21 March 2024, the paper presents pesticide testing and equipment refinement as future work, without establishing later outcomes.

topics.label: Innoshima automatic spraying trial
topics.description:
The automatic-flight variant of the citrus spraying study was conducted with Sanwa Farm on sloping orchard terrain on Innoshima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture, on 19 September 2023. The wire-supplied drone first took off and moved to the start point under manual PosHold control, then followed an automatic route while spraying water. Landing was also manual because hoses and cables could catch the fence between the operating areas.

The paper reports good agreement between the planned and actual automatic-flight path, with pitch kept near horizontal during spraying through RTK-GNSS positioning and recoil cancellation. This demonstrates the reported flight-control behaviour in that test; it does not demonstrate fully autonomous operation from takeoff to landing. Water-sensitive-paper deposition results are described for the separate manual trial, and no automatic-trial tree-survival or irrigation-efficiency outcome is reported. Pesticide testing and later operational performance are not established by the reviewed paper.

topics.label: Ikuchijima manual spraying trial
topics.description:
The manual-flight variant of the citrus spraying study took place with Harada Farm on Ikuchijima Island on 20 September 2023. Takeoff, spraying flight and landing used manual piloting in PosHold mode. A crawler UGV carried the power cable and water hose and was designed to follow the drone when separation exceeded five metres. The experiment tested whether stable water spraying could reach citrus canopies while the tilt mechanism countered recoil.

The paper reports good pitch tracking and recoil cancellation. Water-sensitive paper placed within the trees recorded deposition, including several adhesion indices of 10; the authors concluded that the water adhered well. This is local canopy-deposition evidence, not proof of uniform coverage of every tree, pesticide effectiveness, root-zone delivery or establishment survival. The article also uses the spelling Ikuchishima. Results belong to this September 2023 trial, published in March 2024; pesticide experiments and later equipment refinement remained future work in that source.
